Thirty Years Ahead
Click 🎧 to listen.
Listen to a conversation between two students. The girl is discussing her opinion about the movement to end slavery. Listen carefully. You will hear the conversation only once. After listening, you will answer four questions about the conversation and the evidence the girl gives to support her opinion. As you listen, you may take notes.
Listen to the Conversation
1QUESTION 1:
Why does the girl tell the boy about Britain ending slavery in 1833?
2QUESTION 2:
Where did the girl learn the facts she copied into the spellbook?
3QUESTION 3:
What does the girl say happened when Frederick Douglass went to Britain?
4QUESTION 4:
What does the girl mean when she says the fight to end slavery crossed the ocean?
Answer all 4 questions to submit.
Choose the best answer for each question. You may change your answers before submitting.
SMART SUPPORT:
Go back to the conversation. Identify why the girl brings up Britain. Identify where the facts came from. Identify what the people there did for Frederick Douglass. Identify her main point about ending slavery.
